frontline_communication.snippet:
DO NOT DO BUSINESS WITH AIRTRON.

I went with this company, as they were the provider our homebuilder contracted with. We called to schedule service for an odor when running the AC. The technician arrived 12/26/25 not knowing the reason for the visit. The technician didn't have any knowledge of the Essential HomeCare plan i signed up for. He informed me he was scheduled for a heating service call, when I reported to the service center it was an A/c issue.

I should have refused service right then.

Instead I allowed the tech to service the unit, as he was already there. Maybe he would find a cause. After some amount of time, he finished up, shook my hand and was off. No issue resolution, just that he cleaned out one of the intakes. When i asked about a bill or invoice for services rendered, he said i would get an email. Never got one.

A few weeks later when going into the attic to put away holiday decorations, I discovered two issues. First, the technician had displaced one of the ducts, and had not reseated it properly, and it was allowing air to escape into the attic space, and it was causing a whistling noise. Second, the technician decided to literally dump the debris, dead bugs, etc. from the intake canister right into the attic space. Right onto the insulation.

I have subsequently called Airtron three times, to get ahold of the field supervisor to discuss the situation, unprofessionalism, and complete lack of customer care. No call back. And the office staff had the nerve to say I would need to pay a cancelation fee. What a joke.

I will never recommend anyone to do business with Airtron. What a disappointment and failure of customer service.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Contradictory information between what the customer reported to the service center and what the dispatched technician was told.
frontline_communication.quote: He informed me he was scheduled for a heating service call, when I reported to the service center it was an A/c issue.

frontline_communication.snippet: I had my annual maintenance check up in November and they found a leak in a coil. Dominic Fox came the next week to replace the coil. What should have taken around two hours took four. Dominic pumped too much Freon into my system, causing high pressure and had to call another tech out to my home to figure out the issue. He did not keep me updated on the job and had to call for help without telling me - I realized there was an issue when another tech showed up to my home unannounced. Not only was Dominic uncommunicative and ill equipped to complete the work, but he left a mess by my driveway next to the unit. There was debris everywhere, he left my lockbox unlocked, my electric box open, and drove through the driveway divider gravel with the truck. Before he finished the job, he came into my house and asked if he could heat up his lunch in my microwave. He was more concerned with eating than finishing the job at hand. I was frustrated, but ultimately let it go until a couple of weeks later, I went into my attic to change my HVAC filter. I was horrified to see that he left trash and debris everywhere, including a can in my insulation! He was drinking a beverage in my attic while he worked and tossed in into my insulation. He was so disrespectful toward my home, treating it like a trash can. The photos attached are just some of the screws, zip ties, washers, boxes, plastic, cans, etc. I cleaned up from my attic. I called customer service and asked to speak to the service manager Javier. The customer service rep noted my concerns and said Javier would give me a call back. Javier never got back to me. I’m upset that a company would show up to my home and disrespect it like this and furthermore, no service manager has taken the time to follow up with me. I have been telling my neighbors about my negative experience and I’d recommend anyone to look elsewhere for their HVAC services.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Missing information during the job; customer only learned of a problem when a second tech showed up unannounced.
frontline_communication.quote: He did not keep me updated on the job and had to call for help without telling me

frontline_communication.snippet:
Very poor communication and unprofessional service. I waited over a month for parts with no proactive updates, and when the technician finally arrived, the experience raised serious concerns about both professionalism and preparedness.

I originally scheduled a morning appointment for dehumidifier installation, UV light installation, and coil cleaning. After waiting until nearly 11:00 AM with no update, I called and was told they were waiting on parts (UV light) and would not be coming. No one notified me in advance, and no timeline was provided.

Over the next month, I followed up a couple times and was initially told they were waiting on the UV light. When they later called to schedule, they stated the dehumidifier had arrived and that was what they had been waiting on, which was inconsistent with the earlier updates.

When the technician (Angel) arrived, he immediately displayed a negative attitude. There was confusion about the attic access, and he expressed concern about getting the dehumidifier into the attic due to space constraints.

When I attempted to go up to the attic to show him the access and layout, he raised his voice and said, “Don’t come up here, you don’t need to be here.” This was unnecessary and unprofessional, particularly given that it is my home and I routinely access the attic myself (e.g., for filter changes).

When I asked about the UV light installation, he admitted he had only been told to “change a bulb” and was unsure how to install the unit. He also stated he did not know where the air return was, which raised concerns about preparedness.

He made multiple trips back to his van with no clear plan. I was also concerned about them unpacking and moving the dehumidifier inside before confirming it could be brought up to the attic, so I asked what the process would look like and noted that the attic pull-down stairs may not support the combined weight of the technician and the unit. He did not provide a clear explanation and instead responded, “I’ll figure it out once we get it moved in here.” When I tried to ask follow-up questions to understand the plan, his responses were abrupt and dismissive, and he appeared unwilling to answer basic questions about the work being performed in my home.

He then asked me to open the garage door and pulled down the attic stairs without clearly explaining what he was doing.

During this process, my back door was scratched.

My appointment window was 8:00 AM-1:00 PM, but he did not arrive until around 3:00 PM and spent another hour trying to figure things out. I had already rearranged my day and could not continue waiting, and I was no longer comfortable proceeding.

A neighbor later described a very similar experience involving a technician with the same type of behavior - dismissive, uncommunicative, and only willing to speak to her husband, which suggests this may not be an isolated issue.

Overall, the lack of communication, inconsistent information, questionable preparedness, and poor customer service caused me to lose trust in AirTron
frontline_communication.reasoning: Contradictory explanations from staff about what part the job was waiting on.
frontline_communication.quote: they stated the dehumidifier had arrived and that was what they had been waiting on, which was inconsistent with the earlier updates

Now that the weather has changed, we turned on our heat and discovered it wasn’t working. We were freezing for two days. Thankfully, they sent Jeffery back out, and he found the issue there was a wire that had not been reconnected. On top of that. The previous crew left their trash and empty water bottles in our home that we didn't notice until we went to try to find out why the heat was not coming on. We try but we couldn't figure it out.

Because of all this, we will be looking for a company that actually values and appreciates its customers.

followup_dropped.snippet:
At the end of May, Texas HVAC came out under a home warranty claim for our AC not cooling properly. The technician cleaned the drain lines, replaced the capacitor, and then recommended installing a hard start kit to reduce strain on the unit. Fast forward to this week—just two months later—and our AC completely stops working again. We called Texas HVAC directly, only to be told they only warranty work done for home warranty claims for 30 days. We opened a new claim through our warranty company, and a different company came out. That technician immediately discovered that the hard start kit installed by Texas HVAC had exploded and melted, damaging the wiring and rendering the entire unit inoperable (see pictures). We contacted Texas HVAC to inform them of the issue and were told a manager would call us back. No one called. We followed up the next day—again told a manager would return our call. Still nothing. On the third day, after saying we are willing to drive to their office if their staff is that busy, someone finally called—but it was a technician, not a manager. Instead of offering help, we got a five-minute lecture about how “this happens a lot of the time with these items for various reasons.” We were then told they don’t warranty that part after 30 days, even though it was recommended and installed by their technician.  No help. No discount. No accountability. Just a shrug.  Meanwhile, we’re now on day five with no AC in the middle of a Texas summer, working to source parts and repair the damage they caused.

It’s incredibly frustrating that they would recommend and install a part that failed so catastrophically—and then refuse to stand behind their work or help make it right. I would not trust this company with your HVAC system or your home.

booking_friction.snippet:
I was very impressed with the Dallas Air Clinic's quality of work replacing 2 HVAC units replaced in 2019.  The main salesman they had at that time could sell ice cubes in Antarctica, and made sure the installation team did everything he promised.  I really was impressed with this company.

Fast forward to 2026.  I called them for a tune up on both units, since I had such a good experience with them before and I got a mailer that advertised $69 tune ups.  Great!  I trust this company even though both units had been tuned up since then by other companies.

The day of the service call, they called 2 hours into the window with a sob story of how they've been inundated with emergency calls and needed to reschedule.  Even though I arranged to be home all day that day, and temperatures were in the mid 70s that week (Emergency, really?)

I agreed because a tune-up really is not an emergency, even though my time is valuable, but I decided to just let it go.

3 days later, the day of the rescheduled tune up:  The technician that showed up was certainly polite and personable.  Found several parts that supposedly needed replacing.  OK, that is to be expected.

My big complaint is that the final invoice I received had no prices listed for each individual part replaced, or even for the actual tune up or labor costs, but rather simply listed a grand total for the whole thing.  After calling and complaining, I was told "we don't list prices because we don't charge sales tax".  Huh?  What does that have to do with the price of tea in China?  That seems more like a scheme to charge $350 for a $15 part, and hope nobody notices. No breakdown whatsoever between parts, labor, tune-up, or service call.

Additionally, around lunch time the technician conveniently announced he had run out of refrigerant and needed to leave and go get more.  Disappeared for about 45 minutes.  Refrigerant or a burger while charging time?

After going outside to inspect the compressor units afterwards, I found the fins on the compressor unit were never even rinsed off.

Needless to say, I will not be using Air Clinic anymore.
booking_friction.reasoning: Company cancelled mid-window after customer arranged to be home all day; a single reschedule, so no listed sub precisely fits.
booking_friction.quote: they called 2 hours into the window with a sob story of how they've been inundated with emergency calls and needed to reschedule

frontline_communication.snippet: Have been a long time strickland customer. I used to admire their honest service calls and have recomended them to several family members and neighbors over the years. As members, we would get semi-annual service check ups, the last one being in May of 2025. In December of 2025, we noticed our ceiling right below our unit began to leak. We called strickland as this was a HVAC related leak coming out of the drip pan they installed a few years prior. One of their service members came out and stated that the drain pipes were cleared and that the leak is happening because the unit pendulum was strapped in horizontally and was slowly sinking down and crushing the drip pan. This was a complete lie as the pendulum is very clearly strapped vertically to the attic ceiling and is nowhere near "crushing" the pan they had installed. The leak stopped while they were there as AC was not running during this time. The tech that came out sat me and my wife down and wasted an hour of our time trying to pitch us getting a whole new unit as they could not pinpoint what the exact issue was. We obviously got a second opinion and it turned out that our drain pipes were clogged (creating water back up) and the drip pan strickland installed was not leveled causing any excess water to easily leak out of the side. In addition, there were no gaskets or sealant installed on this drip pan where the piping exit cutouts were located making it much easier for excess water to leak out of the pan. Stricklands failure to properly install a drip pan at level and identify that water was backed up in the unit and not flowing through the drain pipes has caused serious damage to our ceiling. Strickland does not take any responsibility for this. As a matter of fact they get very defensive whenever a complaint is brought up. We've had good experiences with them in the past and a couple questionable experiences but this has sealed the deal.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Customer raised a specific damage complaint and the company refused responsibility and reacted defensively rather than addressing it.
frontline_communication.quote: they get very defensive whenever a complaint is brought up
